title: Balance family exposure so gains transfer better
summary: If practice is dominated by one family, the player may build narrow strength that does not hold up well in other aim demands.
why: Transfer usually improves when the player keeps one strong family while feeding a smaller contrast family alongside it.
The goal is not equal time everywhere; it is enough contrast to stop adaptation from becoming too narrow.
actions: Keep the main family as the anchor, then add one supporting family that challenges the opposite weakness.
Review the weakest family for movement qualities that are missing from the main block.
Use contrast work consistently for a week before judging whether it is helping.
avoid: Do not swing from over-specialized practice to completely random scenario selection.

drills.label: Contrast family block

drills.reason: A contrast block broadens adaptation without discarding the main training theme.

evidence.claim: Practice transfer improves when an anchor family is paired with a purposeful contrast family.
